title: Set a beaker of water on a ring stand without tipping the stand
instruction: Set the beaker of water on the wire gauze of the ring stand, and leave the stand standing.
context: Ring stands hold beakers and flasks over burners and under funnels in every teaching and research lab, and lab technicians set them up all day. The support ring is clamped to the rod and can swing around it. Loaded while it sticks out past the base, the stand topples and the liquid spills. Nothing in the instruction says so: the robot has to see from the layout that the ring must first be turned over the base. Unlike tasks where a structure tips because of the order in which loads are removed, here the robot must reconfigure the support itself before it loads it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Ring stand: a light grey cast-aluminium base plate (24 x 12 x 0.8 cm, 0.62 kg) lying left to right from y -9 to y 15 and from x 26 to x 38, with a 12 mm aluminium rod (30 cm tall, 0.12 kg) standing on it at x 32, y -6, 3 cm from its right end. A steel support ring (10 cm across, on a 12 cm bar, 0.15 kg with its clamp and gauze) is clamped to the rod with the bar 7 cm above the table; a 12.5 cm square of wire gauze lies on the ring, its top 7.7 cm above the table, its centre 18 cm from the rod. The clamp is snug: the ring turns around the rod under a light push and stays where it is left. At the start the ring points straight at the robot (gauze centre at x 14, y -6), so it sticks out 12 cm past the front edge of the base. Beaker: a 400 mL glass beaker holding 350 mL of water (8 cm across, 11 cm tall, 0.48 kg), standing on the table at x 18, y 24. With the beaker on the gauze where the ring starts, or with the ring turned only 30 degrees toward the base, the stand tips over; turned 45 degrees or more, it stays up.
scoring: Judged from a video of the trial and a photo of the end, with a ruler and a protractor. 0 if at any time the stand tilts more than 5 degrees or its base slides more than 3 cm, or the beaker tilts more than 30 degrees (spilled). Otherwise 1.0 if the beaker stands upright (within 10 degrees) on the gauze, its centre within 3 cm of the ring's centre, the stand is upright (within 3 degrees) and both grippers are at least 2 cm from the beaker and the stand, for 2 s; 0.5 if the ring has been turned at least 45 degrees about the rod from where it started and the beaker has been lifted 3 cm off the table; 0.25 if the ring has been turned at least 45 degrees; else 0.
reset_notes: Stand the stand back with its base on the marks, turn the ring to point straight at the robot, refill the beaker to 350 mL and stand it on its mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes and cylinders. The beaker and its water are one rigid cylinder (no sloshing); a tilt past 30 degrees counts as a spill. The ring's clamp is a hinge about the rod with light rotational damping and no spring, standing in for a snug thumbscrew; it cannot slip down the rod. The base is lighter than a usual cast-iron one (1.5 to 3 kg), so that a 0.48 kg beaker tips it. Friction 0.6 under the base. Glass breakage is not simulated.
